content: Search results were thin (generic TTL/Redis advice only). Sound engineering default for a localhost API reading small JSON state files rewritten by external scripts: since writers use same-dir temp + os.replace (atomic), readers never observe partial files, so per-request json.load is correct and cheap at single-user QPS; no cache needed. If caching is desired, key on os.stat mtime so a changed file invalidates immediately, never a fixed TTL alone. Report freshness (file mtime / age) in API responses so consumers can judge staleness - matches repo's data-freshness discipline.
